ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the diagram: the gray horizontal belt in the diagram represents a "pressure belt", and the position marked M is on the gray pressure belt in Figure ①, with the "30°" latitude marker visible beside it. Then reason: according to the distribution pattern of global pressure belts, near the equator is the equatorial low pressure belt, near 30° north and south latitude is the subtropical high pressure belt, and near 60° north and south latitude is the subpolar low pressure belt.
